Secrets just past each bound of the exceptions for code that make the shapes
of oracle_gaps.txt, as secrets of a class whose name starts with
oracle_near_. A bound is one condition of floorValue or plainCode in
redact.go, or of a predicate they call, that limits an exception: a
character class, a length, a count or a refusal. oracleBounds in
oracle_bounds_test.go lists every one, with what it says, changes of
redact.go that widen the exception past it alone, and a generator of near
cases. Each case here is a labelled near case of one bound: its name starts
with the bound's id and a colon, and one case of each bound has the text of
the bound's example; a bound with more than one widening has a case each
widening keeps. There the exception does not hold, and the current rules
alone remove the secret today as the baseline rules do. Where the value
rules would take the secret before the floor is asked, the case would hold
nothing, so each case stands where the value rules read code and only the
floor's exception refuses it.

A gap class excuses its whole shape, so without these a rule change that
widened an exception past one of its bounds would keep secrets the baseline
rules remove and TestOracle would not see it. They are held to the baseline
like any class that is no gap. The bounds of floorValue hold for every
shape; their near cases stand in the near class of yaml_alias or
name_index. See README.md for the format.
